correctness.rationale: For every r>=2, each Q(i,a) consists of 2r+4 pairwise conflicting edges, forcing 2r+4 colors. Assuming equality, all leaf-cycle edges at a fixed index have one color. Summation over six saturated cliques gives 2S+3H+E=6 per color. The cycle-induced-matching bound H,E<=2 and interval forbiddance of four spoke layers exclude every E>0 case, contradiction. An explicit 9-color table for r=2 and a two-fresh-color leaf-extension induction attain 2r+5 for all r. Restriction to a star edge-subgraph gives the general-graph lower bound. A standalone actual-edge checker verified all constructed colorings for r=2..30 and all local clique edges for r=2..7; the proof does not extrapolate these checks.

originality.rationale: The 2021 preprint / 2022 article by Dara, Mishra, Narayanan and Tuza gives a 2Δ+4 lower and 2Δ+6 upper bound for tree-by-C6 products and states the r=2 exact value 9. Inspecting its full accessible article, especially Section 5, found no exact r>=3 star formula or all-graph lower bound. The new local saturation argument forces 2r+5 and gives a sharp general lower bound beyond that result. Searches across terminology and mathematical records produced no equivalent theorem. This is best-knowledge originality, not independent publication-priority certification.
residual_risks: Unindexed, inaccessible, or differently titled published work might already imply the result; originality has not been independently certified.

value.rationale: The natural six-cycle case lies outside the established 4-divisible exact tree-product theorem. The result resolves every member of a nontrivial infinite two-parameter-degree star family from an explicit three-value prior interval, and strengthens the universal lower bound for every graph with maximum degree at least two. The saturation identity explains an intrinsic cyclic obstruction and the leaf-extension rule attains it. This is a structural exact result, not a mere small-case computation.
